# ThimbleDB contribution guidance

Public documentation, website copy, examples, release notes, commit messages,
and pull request descriptions must use neutral open-source project language.

- Address application developers and operators directly.
- Do not write owner-facing QA reports, private handoffs, or conversational
  status summaries into public project files.
- Keep technical claims tied to checked-in tests, source, or raw evidence.
- Separate verified behaviour from expected or unproven benefits.
- State rejection criteria and poor-fit workloads clearly.
- Keep `docs/`, the static website, starter examples, package exports, and
  `llms.txt` discovery files consistent when public behaviour changes.
- Do not add Copilot as an author, co-author, or reviewer.
